scope: Targeted canonical-date fixes for seven flagged source IDs in four reports; dependent claims removed or replaced using own-date eligible evidence. No claim of exhaustive original-article-vintage verification.

changes.before: The anti-price-war campaign is beginning to appear in the behaviour of major platforms. Bloomberg reported Alibaba and Meituan promising to cease their price war after Beijing's warnings. A reduction in subsidy competition could improve the value of an existing customer relationship even without a sharp rise in national consumption. That makes platform economics a more specific opportunity than the broad growth trade. The qualification is execution: a promise to compete less aggressively must survive the incentive to regain market share. Technology sovereignty adds another layer. Reuters reported Chinese AI firms forming domestic alliances, while Nvidia denied security backdoors after China raised concerns over its chips. Local substitution and access to foreign technology can coexist uneasily; avoid treating either as a settled winner. [[n1316]] [[n1146]] [[n1373]]
changes.after: The investment test for the competition campaign is whether companies change how they win and retain customers. Reuters reported leaders targeting disorderly competition. Less destructive subsidy spending could improve the value of an existing customer relationship even without a sharp rise in national consumption, but that remains an operating hypothesis rather than a completed platform agreement. Look for customer retention and margin improvement before treating policy intent as corporate execution. Technology sovereignty adds another layer. Reuters reported Chinese AI firms forming domestic alliances, while Nvidia denied security backdoors after China raised concerns over its chips. Local substitution and access to foreign technology can coexist uneasily; avoid treating either as a settled winner. [[n1238]] [[n1146]] [[n1373]]
changes.reason: Removed platform pledges whose canonical date is Aug1; retained earlier official competition-policy intent and conditional operating analysis.

changes.before: Australia has a clearer route towards rate relief after the latest inflation evidence. The AFR reported lower inflation setting up an RBA cut, while ABC reported home prices continuing to climb despite the rate pause. That is an important tension for investors: lower inflation can help household purchasing power and funding expectations, yet rising property values can keep the demand response uneven. Mortgage-sensitive businesses should be assessed on the customer's ability and willingness to spend, not simply on the market's preferred policy direction. A rate cut would improve a financing input; it would not guarantee stronger sales for every retailer or repair every household balance sheet. [[n0323]] [[n0351]]
changes.after: Australia has a clearer route towards rate relief after the latest inflation evidence. The AFR reported lower inflation setting up an RBA cut. That improves the financing argument without establishing a broad recovery in household demand. Slower inflation can support purchasing power, but households still need confidence in income and enough cash after essential expenses to spend more. Mortgage-sensitive businesses should therefore be assessed on the customer's ability and willingness to buy, not simply on the market's preferred policy direction. A rate cut would improve a financing input; it would not guarantee stronger sales for every retailer or repair every household balance sheet. [[n0323]]
changes.reason: Removed ABC home-price outcome; exact pre-cutoff publisher availability was not established. Preserved eligible earlier inflation/easing evidence.

changes.before: Alibaba and Meituan promising to end their price war creates a narrower opportunity than betting that the entire Chinese consumer economy is repaired. Bloomberg's report points to a possible change in competition, which can improve the value of existing demand before aggregate spending accelerates. The thesis depends on behaviour following the promise. [[n1316]]
changes.after: Official pressure against disorderly competition creates a potential relative-margin opportunity before broad domestic reflation. Reuters reported leaders promising economic support and a crackdown on that competition. The investment question is whether businesses can earn more from existing demand by retaining customers without indefinitely subsidising each transaction. Policy intent supplies a reason to investigate, not proof that platforms have changed their behaviour. [[n1238]]
changes.reason: Replaced premature Alibaba/Meituan pledges with earlier official policy intent; no platform commitment retained.

changes.before: KWEB or selected platform shares express the opportunity, with competitive and policy risk recognised. A reduction in subsidies can support margins, but a rival seeking market share may reopen the conflict. Avoid describing a policy request as an enforceable floor under profit.
changes.after: KWEB or selected platform shares express the opportunity, with competitive and policy risk recognised. A potential margin benefit requires less subsidy dependence while customer retention holds. If rivals continue competing aggressively, the anticipated profit improvement may fail to arrive even when the policy objective is clear.
changes.reason: Removed implication that a previously halted price war could merely reopen.

changes.before: Add when customer retention and operating margins improve without another subsidy escalation. Abandon the relative-margin argument if competitive spending reaccelerates faster than monetisation.
changes.after: Add when customer retention and operating margins improve without greater subsidy dependence. Abandon the relative-margin argument if competitive spending continues absorbing monetisation benefits. Require operating evidence before treating an official request for restraint as an investable improvement in profit.
changes.reason: Tied trigger to observable future operating evidence rather than an unverified completed pledge.

changes.before: Policy is working through several distinct channels. Reuters reported the childcare-subsidy programme and leaders pledging support while targeting disorderly competition. The household transfer can improve spending capacity; the competition campaign attempts to change the distribution of profit within existing markets. Neither automatically resolves trade uncertainty. The US–China talks left an extension of the truce unresolved, according to CNBC's account, so exporters still face a meaningful event risk. Meanwhile, Bloomberg reported a surprise move to tax bond interest after a long exemption. A change in after-tax return can influence the relative appeal of financial assets, but it is not evidence that investors will shift every affected allocation into equities. Treat the instruments and investor objectives separately. [[n1121]] [[n1131]] [[n1367]]
changes.after: Policy is working through several distinct channels. Reuters reported the childcare-subsidy programme and leaders pledging support while targeting disorderly competition. The household transfer can improve spending capacity; the competition campaign attempts to change the distribution of profit within existing markets. Neither automatically resolves trade uncertainty. The US–China talks left an extension of the truce unresolved, according to CNBC's account, so exporters still face a meaningful event risk. Those differences matter for allocation: direct household support, competitive discipline and trade negotiations reach company earnings through different mechanisms. Prefer a business whose customer demand and cash generation can be assessed under imperfect trade terms rather than assuming every policy channel produces an immediate equity inflow. [[n1121]] [[n1131]] [[n1089]]
changes.reason: Removed surprise bond-interest tax and dependent asset-allocation claim; added already-eligible own-feed citation for the existing truce discussion.

changes.before: Europe is trying to improve the composition and security of investment while demand remains uncertain. Bloomberg reported Germany preparing a fund for strategic assets, and Reuters reported an effort to reduce dependence on China for wind-power components. Those developments identify potential spending channels and supply-chain priorities. They do not establish that every listed industrial company has a funded order or that returns will be attractive at any price. The stronger opportunity is a supplier whose product and capacity match a specific paid need, rather than a broad trade on the size of a policy announcement. [[n3097]] [[n3098]]
changes.after: Europe's investment opportunity increasingly depends on the resilience and economics of its supply chains. Reuters reported Germany aiming to reduce dependence on China for wind-power components. That identifies a procurement priority, rather than a funded order for every domestic supplier. A company's opportunity still depends on whether its product, capacity and costs match a customer's paid need. Prefer an executable project with a credible contractual return to a broad trade on the scale of a policy aspiration. Security of supply can justify additional investment, but the shareholder must still examine who funds it and how much of the value the supplier can retain. [[n3098]]
changes.reason: Removed German strategic-fund announcement and claims depending on its existence; retained earlier wind-component procurement evidence.

changes.before: Australia's equity strength sits alongside practical constraints in housing and construction. ABC reported the housing crisis becoming a construction crisis, highlighting a supply-and-delivery problem that lower financing costs alone may not solve. A household may want a home and obtain a more manageable mortgage while builders still face difficult costs and capacity. Keep the investment distinction clear: demand for housing, developer economics and the affordability of a listed share are related but separate questions. [[n0394]]
changes.after: Australia's domestic-demand case must distinguish slower inflation from a full repair in household purchasing power. The Guardian described inflation falling while prices remained high. That distinction matters for retailers and housing exposure: a slower increase in expenses can improve the direction of household finances without reversing the earlier rise in their cost. Easier financing would help some borrowers, but the benefit still has to become spending at a margin the business can retain. Prefer companies delivering value and generating cash rather than assuming every consumer category rebounds as soon as the rates debate turns friendlier. The equity entry price needs its own justification alongside the customer's capacity to buy. [[n0353]]
changes.reason: Replaced unverified same-date ABC construction outcome with eligible own-date Guardian inflation-versus-price-level headline. Original Guardian publication explicitly precedes cutoff.

changes.before: Reuters asked why the physical oil market remained tight despite large OPEC+ increases. That gives efficient producers a potential upside surprise if realised pricing holds better than futures pessimism implies. Wait for demonstrated cash resilience rather than assuming every supply announcement maps mechanically into realised earnings. [[n6764]]
changes.after: Look for producers able to protect realised cash generation through cost control, disciplined investment and a resilient operating mix. An upside surprise would require those improvements to offset weaker crude assumptions. Add only when results demonstrate that mechanism rather than assuming an announced supply change maps directly into company earnings.
changes.reason: Removed premature physical-oil tightness claim and its claimed upside implication; replaced with a conditional earnings test.
